steps.tx: **Respiratory viral infections** are acute illnesses caused by influenza, SARS-CoV-2, RSV and parainfluenza viruses that infect the upper and lower respiratory tract. Influenza kills about two hundred and ninety thousand to six hundred and fifty thousand people yearly, COVID caused over 7 million deaths by the year two thousand and twenty four, and RSV hospitalises 3 to 5 million children under 5 years annually.
steps.say: Respiratory viral infections are acute illnesses caused by influenza, covid, rsv and parainfluenza viruses. Influenza kills a few hundred thousand people each year. Covid caused over seven million deaths. Rsv hospitalises millions of young children every year.

steps.tx: **Risk factors** for severe respiratory virus disease include age over sixty five years, chronic lung disease, diabetes, obesity with body mass index above 30, pregnancy, and immunosuppression. Household crowding, winter season, and recent hospitalisation also raise risk. About twenty percent of severe COVID cases occur in persons with no classical comorbidity, so exposure alone can be enough.
steps.say: Risk factors are age over sixty five, chronic lung disease, diabetes, obesity, pregnancy and immunosuppression. Crowding, winter season and recent hospital stay raise risk. About twenty percent of severe covid cases have no classical comorbidity. So exposure alone can be enough.

steps.tx: **Viral entry** begins when spike protein binds airway epithelial receptors and the virus replicates in upper then lower airways. Cytokine release injures endothelium, raises capillary leak, and alveoli fill with fluid. Microthrombi form in lung and systemic vessels. This immune injury, not just viral load, produces hypoxaemia, ventilation perfusion mismatch, and acute respiratory distress syndrome in severe cases.
steps.say: Viral entry begins when the spike protein binds airway receptors. The virus replicates first in the upper and then in the lower airways. Cytokine release injures the endothelium and causes capillary leak. Fluid fills the alveoli and microthrombi form. This immune injury causes low oxygen and severe breathing failure.

steps.tx: **Clinical features** begin with fever, cough, coryza, sore throat, myalgia, and headache for 3 to 7 days. Breathlessness, tachypnoea above twenty two per minute, and oxygen saturation below ninety four percent signal lower tract disease. A classic sign is abrupt high fever with severe body aches in influenza, while loss of taste or smell favours COVID. Elderly patients often present as confusion and falls without fever.
steps.say: Symptoms include fever, cough, running nose, sore throat, muscle pain and headache for a few days. Breathlessness and fast breathing warn of lung involvement. Abrupt high fever with severe body ache suggests flu, while loss of taste favours covid. Elderly patients may show confusion without fever.

steps.tx: **Pattern recognition** separates these viruses at the bedside. Influenza peaks in twenty four to forty eight hours with dry cough and prostration. COVID evolves over 7 to 10 days with gastrointestinal symptoms in 15% and lymphopenia. RSV causes wheeze and bronchiolitis in infants below 6 months. Adenovirus causes follicular conjunctivitis with pharyngitis and fever called pharyngoconjunctival fever in hostel outbreaks.
steps.say: Pattern recognition helps at the bedside. Flu starts quickly with dry cough and prostration. Covid evolves slowly over a week or more and often has gut symptoms. Rsv causes wheeze in small infants. Adenovirus causes eye redness with throat infection in hostel outbreaks.

rows: Twenty four to forty eight hours

steps.tx: **First test** is rapid antigen or molecular testing on a nasal swab, while chest X-ray and pulse oximetry grade severity. The gold standard is real time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction showing cycle threshold below 30 with high viral load. D-dimer above one thousand nanograms per millilitre and ferritin above five hundred nanograms per millilitre suggest cytokine storm. Lymphocyte count below one thousand per microlitre predicts deterioration.
steps.say: First do a nasal swab test and check oxygen level and chest x ray. The gold standard is the molecular test showing low cycle threshold. High d dimer and ferritin suggest a cytokine storm. A low lymphocyte count predicts worsening.

steps.tx: **Interpretation** links tests to stage. Early disease shows normal white cells with positive antigen, while severe disease shows lymphopenia, raised interleukin 6, and bilateral ground glass opacities on computed tomography. Blood culture is negative in most pure viral cases, so repeated antibiotics without proof add resistance. A falling oxygen requirement and improving d dimer trend matter more than a single value.
steps.say: Interpret the stage first. Early disease shows positive tests with normal white cells. Severe disease shows lymphopenia, high inflammation markers and ground glass shadowing on scan. Blood cultures are usually negative. Trends in oxygen need matter more than one value.

steps.tx: **First line management** for uncomplicated viral flu is supportive care with fluids, antipyretics, and rest. Early antiviral cover with seventy five milligrams twice daily for 5 days works best within forty eight hours and suits patients above thirteen years. Nirmatrelvir 300 milligrams with ritonavir 100 milligrams twice daily for 5 days suits early COVID in high risk adults. Dexamethasone 6 milligrams daily is reserved for oxygen dependent severe COVID.
steps.say: Support the patient with fluids, fever control and rest. Early antiviral cover is given twice daily for five days and works best within two days. The newer combination pill is given for five days in early high risk covid. Dexamethasone is saved for patients who need oxygen.

steps.tx: **Escalation** uses low molecular weight blood thinning injections, awake proning, and high flow oxygen for hypoxaemia. Tocilizumab 8 milligrams per kilogram single infusion is added only when oxygen need rises with raised inflammatory markers. Remdesivir 200 milligrams on day one then 100 milligrams daily is an option in hospitalised patients. Antibiotics are added only when bacterial superinfection is proven by culture or procalcitonin rise.
steps.say: Escalate with blood thinners, prone positioning and high flow oxygen. Tocilizumab is added only when oxygen need rises with high inflammation. Remdesivir is an option for hospitalised patients. Add antibiotics only when bacterial infection is proven by culture or markers.

steps.tx: **Complications** include secondary bacterial pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in nought point six percent of children. Prognosis is good in young healthy adults but mortality reaches ten to twenty percent in ventilated elderly patients. Long COVID affects 10% of patients with fatigue, brain fog, and dysautonomia for over 12 weeks. Follow up chest imaging at 6 weeks helps detect fibrosis.
steps.say: Complications include bacterial pneumonia, respiratory failure, clots, kidney injury and a multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children. Recovery is good in the young but mortality is high in ventilated elderly patients. Long covid affects one in ten patients. Follow up scans help detect lung fibrosis.

steps.tx: **High-yield for the exam** pairs incubation, drug timing, and steroid rule in one frame. Early antiviral cover within forty eight hours, dexamethasone only with oxygen, and ritonavir interaction checks are favourite stems. Cycle threshold below 30 means high infectivity, while proning improves oxygenation. Remember isolation for 5 days.
steps.say: Keep incubation period, drug timing and the steroid rule in one frame. Early antiviral cover starts early and is given in the first days, while steroids are only with oxygen. Low cycle threshold means high infectivity and isolation is advised after symptoms.
